intro: A Vermont fiddler and banjoist who reinvents traditional songs.
story: Sam Amidon is a Vermont singer, fiddler and banjoist who reimagines traditional folk songs. His Nonesuch debut, Bright Sunny South, came in 2013, and Lily-O, made with the guitarist Bill Frisell, followed in 2014; NPR said he approaches the genre with adventure rather than reverence. He played Pickathon in 2015 and returned in 2018. Salt River came on River Lea in 2025, and Willing Brother Knowing, produced by Big Thief's James Krivchenia, is due in February 2027.
artist_reel_line: Willing Brother Knowing, produced by James Krivchenia, is due in February 2027.

intro: Ahmed Gallab's project of Sudanese pop, funk and krautrock.
story: Sinkane is Ahmed Gallab, a Sudanese-American multi-instrumentalist who toured with Yeasayer, Caribou and Of Montreal before leading his own band. In 2014 he was musical director of the Atomic Bomb! Band shows honoring the Nigerian funk pioneer William Onyeabor, and that year came Mean Love on DFA, which mixes Sudanese rhythms with soul, country and reggae. Sinkane played Pickathon in 2015. Life & Livin' It followed on City Slang in 2017, and in 2026 Gallab announced He's Gone, due in February 2027, with a single featuring Mdou Moctar.
artist_reel_line: He announced He's Gone for February 2027, with a single featuring Mdou Moctar.

intro: A co-founder of the Carolina Chocolate Drops.
story: Dom Flemons co-founded the Grammy-winning Carolina Chocolate Drops and records solo as The American Songster. He was a celebrated torchbearer of old-time string-band music when he played Pickathon in 2015. Black Cowboys, on Smithsonian Folkways in 2018, was nominated for the Grammy for Best Folk Album, and the Living Blues critics' poll honored him in 2019. Traveling Wildfire came in 2023, and in 2026 he announced an album recorded on historic instruments from the Smithsonian's collections.
artist_reel_line: A 2026 album, Making American Music: The Smithsonian Sessions, uses historic instruments.

intro: A North Carolina banjoist and percussionist.
story: Nathan Bowles is a banjoist and percussionist from Durham, North Carolina, who plays in Pelt and the Black Twig Pickers and has backed Steve Gunn. He played Pickathon in 2015, the year after Nansemond. Whole & Cloven, on Paradise of Bachelors in 2016, was the first solo record where he let the banjo guide things without being the center, and Plainly Mistaken came in 2018. In 2026 he returned to Pickathon with solo sets of banjo, tape loops and keyboards.
artist_reel_line: He returned in 2026 with solo sets of banjo, tape loops and keyboards.

story: Shabazz Palaces are Ishmael Butler's Seattle collective, with the multi-instrumentalist Tendai Maraire, signed to Sub Pop; Butler was Butterfly of Digable Planets. They came to Pickathon in 2013 and again in 2015, the year after Lese Majesty, which The Line of Best Fit named Album of the Week. Quazarz came in 2017 and The Don of Diamond Dreams in 2020. Their eighth album, It's A Style Sport, came out on Sub Pop in October 2026.
artist_reel_line: Their eighth album, It's A Style Sport, came out on Sub Pop in October 2026.

intro: A Tuareg collective from northern Mali.
story: Tinariwen are a Tuareg collective from northern Mali, and their 2011 album Tassili won the Grammy for Best World Music Album in 2012. Emmaar, in 2014, was their first album not recorded in northern Africa, made in the California desert with guests including Josh Klinghoffer. They played Pickathon in 2015 and again in 2018. Elwan came in 2017 and Amadjar in 2019. Hoggar, on Wedge in 2026, was followed by tours of Europe and South America.
artist_reel_line: Hoggar came out on Wedge in 2026, followed by tours of Europe and South America.

intro: A Kentucky songwriter of quiet, luminous folk.
story: Joan Shelley is a Louisville songwriter whose quiet folk songs made her a treasured Pickathon visitor in 2015. Over and Even, her third solo album, came out that September on No Quarter, recorded in a cold Kentucky barn with Daniel Martin Moore producing and Will Oldham singing a duet; NPR's Will Hermes counted it among the year's most beautiful releases. Joan Shelley, cut at Wilco's Loft in Chicago, followed in 2017 and Like the River Loves the Sea in 2019. Real Warmth, recorded in Toronto with the producer Ben Whiteley, came in 2025, and she toured through 2026.
artist_reel_line: Real Warmth, recorded in Toronto with Ben Whiteley, came in 2025, then a 2026 tour.

intro: A California fuzz-rock songwriter who records constantly.
story: Ty Segall played Pickathon in 2013, 2015, 2016 and 2017, and in 2015 his set was billed Ty Segall and the Roling Stons. Manipulator, written over 14 months, long by his standards, came out on Drag City in 2014. He kept recording steadily: Freedom's Goblin in 2018, First Taste in 2019, Possession in 2025 and Chrome in 2026, with the companion EP Love Fuzzz and a South American tour in November 2026.
artist_reel_line: Chrome and the EP Love Fuzzz came in 2026, followed by a South American tour.

intro: A Fort Worth soul singer who signed to Columbia in 2014.
story: Leon Bridges, born in Atlanta and raised in Fort Worth, signed to Columbia in December 2014. Coming Home, made at Niles City Sound in Fort Worth with White Denim's Austin Jenkins and Josh Block, came out in June 2015, the year he played Pickathon. It was nominated for Best R&B Album at the 2016 Grammys, and the Americana Music Association nominated him as an emerging act. Good Thing followed in 2018, and its single Bet Ain't Worth the Hand won a Grammy for Best Traditional R&B Performance. Gold-Diggers Sound came in 2021 and Leon in 2024; his fifth album, Happiness Anytime, was co-produced with members of Jungle.
artist_reel_line: Happiness Anytime, co-produced with members of Jungle, brought international tour dates.
